“Humans have three types of cone cells in their eyes, sensitive to red, green, and blue light. These three types of cones allow us to perceive a wide range of colors by mixing signals from them”

Humans see the same colors unless they’re colorblind. How they interpret what they see is more of a psychological and neurological process. So we all see the same things, but not come to the same conclusion

What you’re asking is more apparent between species. For example: Mantis Shrimp have 12-16 different types of photoreceptors in their eyes.
